### Summary

Google Meet node commands could skip exec approvals. In affected versions, `googlemeet.chrome` accepted caller-supplied audio command arrays and executed them on a paired node outside the normal `system.run` approval path.

This advisory is scoped to deployments with the Google Meet plugin enabled, a paired Chrome node, and the node command allowed. Pairing a node remains an operator-level trust decision; the failed boundary is the configured exec approval path for model-triggered commands.

### Impact

A tool-enabled agent able to invoke the allowed Google Meet node command could execute attacker-selected processes on the paired node. This could affect files, credentials, browser profiles, and availability on that node.

### Patched Versions

The first stable patched version is `2026.7.1`.

### Mitigations

upgrade to `openclaw@2026.7.1` or later. Before upgrading, remove `googlemeet.chrome` from allowed node commands or disable the Google Meet plugin.
summary: Google Meet node commands could skip exec approvals
